metadata.description: Compare two values and return a Comparison.
comments: compare(x, y) returns the hydra.core.util.Comparison value that classifies the relationship between x and y under the type's ordering: LessThan if x < y, EqualTo if x == y, GreaterThan if x > y.
The result type's three-valued tag is the canonical primitive comparison; the boolean comparators (lt/lte/gt/gte) are derivable from it.
Requires an 'ordering' type-class constraint on the argument type, which is the closest Hydra equivalent to Haskell's Ord instance.
Since: 0.18 (moved from hydra.core.lib.equality.compare).
Total. Corresponds to Haskell's compare :: Ord a => a -> a -> Ordering.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.ordering.compare.threeWayClassification
provisions.statement: compare(x, y) returns lessThan, equalTo, or greaterThan classifying x relative to y under the type's ordering, for integers, strings (lexicographic, by Unicode code point), floats, lists (lexicographic, order-sensitive), sets, and maps (canonical sorted-order comparison, independent of construction/insertion order).

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.ordering.compare.decimalScaleTiebreak
provisions.statement: compare on decimals orders primarily by numeric value; when two decimals are numerically equal but have different scale, compare treats them as distinct (not equalTo) and breaks the tie by scale (smaller scale orders first), including transitively across more than two scale levels.

metadata.description: Check whether the first value is greater than the second.
comments: gt(x, y) returns true iff x > y under the type's ordering.
Requires an 'ordering' constraint on the argument type.
Since: 0.18 (moved from hydra.core.lib.equality.gt).
Total. Corresponds to Haskell's (>) :: Ord a => a -> a -> Bool.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.ordering.gt.strictGreaterThan
provisions.statement: gt(x, y) returns true exactly when x is strictly greater than y under the type's ordering, for integers, floats, and strings; equal values and lesser values both return false.

metadata.description: Check whether the first value is greater than or equal to the second.
comments: gte(x, y) returns true iff x >= y under the type's ordering.
Requires an 'ordering' constraint on the argument type.
Since: 0.18 (moved from hydra.core.lib.equality.gte).
Total. Corresponds to Haskell's (>=) :: Ord a => a -> a -> Bool.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.ordering.gte.greaterThanOrEqual
provisions.statement: gte(x, y) returns true when x is greater than or strictly equal to y under the type's ordering, for integers, floats, strings, and decimals -- including the decimal scale-tiebreak rule (a numerically-equal, smaller-scale decimal is treated as lesser, so gte is true in that direction).

metadata.description: Check whether the first value is less than the second.
comments: lt(x, y) returns true iff x < y under the type's ordering.
Requires an 'ordering' constraint on the argument type.
Since: 0.18 (moved from hydra.core.lib.equality.lt).
Total. Corresponds to Haskell's (<) :: Ord a => a -> a -> Bool.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.ordering.lt.strictLessThan
provisions.statement: lt(x, y) returns true exactly when x is strictly less than y under the type's ordering, for integers, floats, and strings; equal values and greater values both return false.

metadata.description: Check whether the first value is less than or equal to the second.
comments: lte(x, y) returns true iff x <= y under the type's ordering.
Requires an 'ordering' constraint on the argument type.
Since: 0.18 (moved from hydra.core.lib.equality.lte).
Total. Corresponds to Haskell's (<=) :: Ord a => a -> a -> Bool.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.ordering.lte.lessThanOrEqual
provisions.statement: lte(x, y) returns true when x is less than or strictly equal to y under the type's ordering, for integers, floats, strings, and decimals -- including the decimal scale-tiebreak rule.

metadata.description: Return the maximum of two values.
comments: max(x, y) returns the larger of x and y under the type's ordering; if x == y, it returns y (matching Haskell's convention).
Requires an 'ordering' constraint on the argument type.
Since: 0.18 (moved from hydra.core.lib.equality.max).
Total. Corresponds to Haskell's max :: Ord a => a -> a -> a.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.ordering.max.returnsLargerOperand
provisions.statement: max(x, y) returns whichever of x and y is larger under the type's ordering; when x and y are equal, max returns y (matching Haskell's tie-breaking convention) -- holds for integers, strings, floats, and decimals.

metadata.description: Return the minimum of two values.
comments: min(x, y) returns the smaller of x and y under the type's ordering; if x == y, it returns x (matching Haskell's convention).
Requires an 'ordering' constraint on the argument type.
Since: 0.18 (moved from hydra.core.lib.equality.min).
Total. Corresponds to Haskell's min :: Ord a => a -> a -> a.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.ordering.min.returnsSmallerOperand
provisions.statement: min(x, y) returns whichever of x and y is smaller under the type's ordering; when x and y are equal, min returns x (matching Haskell's tie-breaking convention) -- holds for integers, strings, floats, and decimals.
